title: Tamsin and the Alibi
premise: Paloma Sterling, the concierge at the Meridian Hotel, has built her career on noticing what guests want to hide. When a nervous stranger named Tamsin pays a month in advance for one service: prove that hotel owner Edmund Voss will not be murdered on the night of the spring tide. Paloma's investigation reveals Voss is already planning his own death — a staged murder to frame his business partner and expose a ledger of bribes hidden in the hotel's reservation system. But when the night arrives and Voss turns up genuinely dead, Paloma must decide whether to protect Tamsin, who is Voss's estranged daughter living under a false identity, or hand the truth to a police force already bought by the partner. In the end, Paloma decodes the ledger, lets the tide return the evidence Voss hid beneath the pier, and chooses justice outside the law — clearing Tamsin's name while letting the town believe its comfortable lie.
about_author: Gideon Villalobos is a former night auditor at coastal hotels who claims he wrote his first mystery on the backs of guest registration cards. He lives in a fog-bound port town where he still greets strangers by guessing their room preferences.

chapters.title: The Guest Who Paid for Nothing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A woman calling herself Tamsin checks into the Meridian and pre-pays for an impossible service: proof that a murder will not happen. Paloma's professional curiosity wars with her instinct that this guest is lying about everything except her fear. Beat: intrigue and unease.

chapters.title: Five Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with flashback. We learn how a concierge becomes the keeper of a town's confessions — affairs, debts, disappearances — filed in her memory like a card catalog. She runs a quiet background check on Tamsin and finds the identity is paper-thin. Beat: establishment of Paloma's power and loneliness.

chapters.title: Edmund Voss Drinks Alone
chapters.summary: Paloma observes Voss, the hotel's owner, behaving strangely: settling debts, burning papers, booking a suite under a name she's never seen him use. He seems to be preparing for something. The spring tide is ten days out. Beat: dread disguised as routine.

chapters.title: A Ledger Hidden in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Tamsin finally explains: Voss keeps a coded ledger of bribes woven into the hotel's reservation records — dates, room numbers, guest initials. If he dies before revealing it, the corruption dies with him and the town stays rotten. Beat: the mystery acquires stakes beyond one man.

chapters.title: Room 214, Booked Forever
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She begins decoding the reservation system and finds Room 214 has been booked continuously for six years under rotating fake names — always paid from the same account. Someone powerful has been renting silence. Beat: first real discovery, rising tension.

chapters.title: The Partner Who Smiles Too Much
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Business partner Aldous Crane notices her questions and responds with charm edged in threat, offering her a promotion to stop looking. She accepts the drink, declines the offer, and notes his cufflinks match payments in the ledger. Beat: the antagonist steps forward.

chapters.title: What the Tide Takes
chapters.summary: Paloma walks the pier at low tide where Voss was seen burying something years ago. She finds a rusted strongbox bolted beneath the pilings — too heavy to move alone, too deliberate to be accidental. Beat: physical evidence enters the story; foreboding.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Real Name
chapters.summary: Paloma confronts Tamsin with what she's found: Tamsin is Voss's daughter, presumed dead after a boating accident five years ago — the same year the ledger began. Her return is the variable Voss never planned for. Beat: betrayal and reluctant intimacy between the two women.

chapters.title: The Night of the Spring Tide
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, tense and compressed. Voss stages his own 'murder' as planned — but something goes wrong. Gunshot, screaming, and when Paloma reaches the suite, Voss is dead for real and Tamsin is standing over him holding the prop gun. Beat: the pivot from mystery to crisis.

chapters.title: Alibi
chapters.summary: Interrogation chapter. The police — quietly on Crane's payroll — build their case against Tamsin. Paloma lies smoothly, five years of practice, giving Tamsin an alibi she isn't sure is true. Beat: love against duty crystallizes; Paloma crosses her own line.

chapters.title: Crane's Generosity
chapters.summary: Crane offers to make the charges vanish if Paloma hands over whatever Voss left her — proving he knows more about the staging than an innocent man should. She plays dumb and realizes he thinks the ledger is a physical book. Beat: cat-and-mouse sharpens.

chapters.title: The Reservation Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Paloma digs into the system and finds a booking for tonight, Room 214, made by Voss himself weeks ago — a message scheduled like a dead man's switch. The confirmation code is the key to the cipher. Beat: hope rekindled through method.

chapters.title: Decoding the Guest Book
chapters.summary: Paloma and Tamsin work through the night translating reservations into names, dates, payments — judges, councilmen, the police chief himself. The town's respectability is a fiction maintained by Room 214. Beat: revelation on a grand scale; the women become partners.

chapters.title: The Chief Knows
chapters.summary: Police Chief Marrero summons Paloma privately — not to arrest her, but to warn her. He's in the ledger too, and he's terrified of Crane, not loyal to him. He gives her forty-eight hours before he must act. Beat: moral complexity; even the corrupt have fears.

chapters.title: Someone Checks Out Early
chapters.summary: A witness who could corroborate Tamsin's account — a chambermaid who saw Crane near the suite — disappears. Paloma finds her car at the pier and understands Crane is cleaning house. Beat: escalating danger; the clock tightens.

chapters.title: Under the Pilings
chapters.summary: Paloma and Tamsin return at low tide with tools and take the strongbox: inside, Voss's confession, insurance photos, and a letter naming Tamsin as his heir and his conscience. Voss staged his death to force the ledger into daylight — Crane simply moved faster. Beat: grief and clarity entwined.

chapters.title: The Trap in Suite Nine
chapters.summary: Paloma sets her own stage: she lets Crane believe the ledger is in the hotel safe and lures him into confessing on a recorded line, using the concierge trick of making a guilty man feel clever. Beat: reversal of power; Paloma weaponizes hospitality.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Climax. Crane realizes the trap and comes for the strongbox at the pier as the tide rises. A violent confrontation in the water; Tamsin saves Paloma; Crane is caught by arriving officers — Chief Marrero, choosing at last, plays the recording. Beat: catharsis through action.

chapters.title: What the Town Wanted to Believe
chapters.summary: Fallout. The ledger goes to a state prosecutor, not the local press. Some officials fall; others negotiate immunity. The town prefers the story that Voss died of a heart condition. Paloma must choose: full truth or livable peace. Beat: bittersweet moral weight.

chapters.title: Checkout
chapters.summary: Tamsin, cleared and renamed once more, prepares to leave the town that buried her twice. She asks Paloma to come with her. Paloma looks at the front desk, her files, her alphabetized life. Beat: tender decision point; identity theme peaks.

chapters.title: The Concierge Who Noticed Everything
chapters.summary: Resolution. Paloma stays — but differently: she mails copies of the decoded ledger to every household, ending the culture of secrets she once profited from. The Meridian gets a new owner; Paloma gets a new job title and an open door. Beat: quiet transformation.

chapters.title: Postscript: A Booking Under a New Name
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Paloma's POV. Months later, a reservation arrives: two guests, one week, paid in advance, no name needed. Paloma smiles, keys the room, and leaves a note — 'Welcome back.' Beat: love against duty resolved into love chosen freely.
